```{r}
library(dplyr)
data1990 <- read.csv("housing.csv")
data2024 <- read.csv("LA_Property_Listing.csv") %>% na.omit() %>% filter(price >= 200000)
```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(maps)
gdf <- st_as_sf(data1990, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

#download california county shapes
ca_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codeforamerica/click_that_hood/master/public/data/california-counties.geojson"
counties <- st_read(ca_url)

#use la only
la_boundary <- counties %>% filter(name == "Los Angeles")

#Filter points that are inside the LA boundary
la_points <- st_intersection(gdf, la_boundary)

data1990 <- la_points %>%
  mutate(
    longitude = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1],
    latitude = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2]
  ) %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  relocate(longitude, latitude, .before = 1)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
data2024$price_scaled <- data2024$price / 100000 

counties <- map_data("county")
la_county <- counties %>% filter(region == "california", subregion == "los angeles")
ggplot() + 
  geom_polygon(data = la_county, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group), 
               fill = "gray95", color = "black") +
  geom_point(data = data2024, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = price_scaled), alpha = 0.5, size = 1) + 
  scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("blue", "green", "yellow", "orange", "red"),
  name = "Price ($100k)",
  values = c(0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5,1)) +
  coord_fixed(1.3) + # Keeps the map from looking "stretched"
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Empirical Median House Values in LA County",
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")
```

```{r}
data1990$price_scaled <- data1990$median_house_value / 100000 

counties <- map_data("county")
la_county <- counties %>% filter(region == "california", subregion == "los angeles")
ggplot() +
```

```{r}
#LA only 2024
library(tigris)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

ca_places <- places(state = "CA", cb = TRUE)

la_city_outline <- ca_places %>% 
  filter(NAME == "Los Angeles")
```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  # Layer 1: The official City of Los Angeles border
  geom_sf(data = la_city_outline, fill = "gray95", color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  
  # Layer 2: Your Housing Data points
  geom_point(data = data2024, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = price_scaled), alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  # Styling
  scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("blue", "green", "yellow", "orange", "red"),
  name = "Price ($100k)",
  values = c(0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5,1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Properties within Los Angeles City Limits",
       subtitle = "Using official US Census Bureau boundaries",
       color = "Price")
```

```{r}
library(gstat)
library(terra)
library(tidyterra)
#Convert your city outline and data to a projected coordinate system
#(Kriging works better with meters/feet than Lat/Long degrees)
la_sf <- st_as_sf(data2024, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) %>% st_transform(2229)

la_border_proj <- ca_places %>% 
  filter(NAME == "Los Angeles") %>%
  st_transform(2229)
```

```{r}
coords <- st_coordinates(la_sf)

la_sf <- la_sf %>%
  mutate(
    x_coord = coords[, "X"],
    y_coord = coords[, "Y"]
  )

#detrend data
v_sample <- variogram(log(price) ~ x_coord + y_coord, la_sf)
plot(v_sample)
```

```{r}
v_fit <- fit.variogram(v_sample, model = vgm(model = "Sph", psill = 0.25, range = 50000, nugget = 0.25))

plot(v_sample, v_fit, main= "Variogram Fit (Distances in Feet)")
```

The variogram tells us how related each point is based on distance.

```{r, warning=FALSE}
r_template <- rast(vect(la_border_proj), res = 1000)
grid_points <- as.points(r_template, values = FALSE) %>%
  st_as_sf()

grid_coords <- st_coordinates(grid_points)

grid_points <- grid_points %>%
  mutate(
    x_coord = grid_coords[, "X"],
    y_coord = grid_coords[, "Y"]
  )

#need to half unique points for kriging, fix same place by averaging
#also helps remove some points to make kriging faster
la_sf_unique <- la_sf %>%
  group_by(x_coord, y_coord) %>%
  summarize(
    price = exp(mean(log(price))), # use geometric mean
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
kriged_res <- krige(log(price) ~ x_coord + y_coord, 
                    locations = la_sf_unique, 
                    newdata = grid_points, 
                    model = v_fit,
                    nmax = 50)
```

```{r}
prediction_raster <- rasterize(vect(kriged_res), r_template, field = "var1.pred")

final_raster <- exp(mask(prediction_raster, vect(la_border_proj)))

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = final_raster) +
  geom_sf(data = la_border_proj, fill = NA, color = "white", size = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "H", 
                       labels = scales::dollar, 
                       na.value = "transparent",
                       values = c(0, 0.1, 0.4, 1)
                       ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "LA Housing Price Surface",
       subtitle = "Kriging Prediction (1,000ft Resolution)",
       fill = "Predicted Price")
```

```{r}
variation_raster <- rasterize(vect(kriged_res), r_template, field = "var1.var")

final_raster <- exp(mask(variation_raster, vect(la_border_proj)))

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = final_raster) +
  geom_sf(data = la_border_proj, fill = NA, color = "white", size = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "H", 
                       labels = scales::dollar, 
                       na.value = "transparent",
                       ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "LA Housing Variation",
       subtitle = "Kriging Variation (1,000ft Resolution)",
       fill = "Variance")
```

```{r}
cv_results <- krige.cv(
  formula = log(price) ~ x_coord + y_coord, 
  locations = la_sf_unique, 
  model = v_fit,
  nmax = 50 # Keep nmax consistent with your map settings
)
```

```{r}
coords <- st_coordinates(cv_results)

cv_results <- cv_results %>%
  mutate(
    x_coord = coords[, "X"],
    y_coord = coords[, "Y"]
  )

cv_to_join <- cv_results %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

la_sf_validated <- la_sf %>%
  left_join(cv_to_join, by = c("x_coord", "y_coord"))

sum(!is.na(la_sf_validated$residual))

la_sf_validated$price_kriged <- exp(la_sf_validated$var1.pred)
```

```{r}
#plot the residuals empirical heatmap
la_sf_validated$a <- la_sf_validated$price - la_sf_validated$price_kriged
ggplot() +
  # Layer 1: The official City of Los Angeles border
  geom_sf(data = la_border_proj, fill = "gray95", color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  # Layer 2: Your Housing Data points
  geom_point(data = la_sf_validated, aes(x = x_coord, y = y_coord, color = a), alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  # Styling
  scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("blue", "green", "yellow", "orange", "red"),
  name = "Price ($)",
  values = c(0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.5,1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Properties Price re-estimation",
       color = "Price")
```

```{r}
library(mlr3)
library(broom)
library(stargazer)
```
```{r}
model <- lm(log(price) ~ price_kriged + livingArea, data = la_sf_validated)
summary(model)
```
```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
plot(model)
```

Note: 659 (838 E 80th St) shows up as an outlier because the price is 11000000. Cross referencing the price with redfin shows the price should actually be 1100000. \\
647 (7342 Haskell Ave) is another outlier. The reason why the price is so cheap is because of the debt the seller has to incur upon purchase of the property.
